Maladaptive Strategies.value: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
Talking with others about the event or its aftermath
Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear
I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
I am permanently an outsider now

vignette: Case Vignette for Marco Marco is a 24-year-old Latin American male who has recently returned from serving in a combat zone. He works as a financial analyst and has been experiencing significant distress since his return home. His trauma stems from a particularly harrowing experience during his deployment, where he witnessed the loss of comrades under intense fire. The vividness of these memories and the way they intrude into his daily life have left him feeling hopeless about the future. Marco often finds himself avoiding any reminders of the event, including open spaces where he feels vulnerable, conversations that might lead to discussions about what happened, and anything that reminds him of those he lost. He has come to believe that talking about it would only make things worse, and so he isolates himself from friends and colleagues. His work as a financial analyst has become increasingly difficult due to these avoidance behaviors. When working in open office spaces or during team meetings, Marco feels intensely anxious and often tries to leave early or avoid certain areas of the office. The clarity with which Marco recalls the traumatic event is striking; his memories are so vivid that they seem to replay in his mind like a film, making it hard for him to distinguish between what happened then and now. These intrusive thoughts often occur without warning, leaving him disoriented and unable to focus on his work or daily activities. For instance, when he hears loud noises similar to gunfire or sees an open space, the memory floods back with such intensity that he feels as though he is right there again. Marco’s sense of self has been profoundly affected by these experiences. He holds deeply negative appraisals about himself and his future. The violence and chaos he witnessed have led him to feel that he acted in ways that violated his core values, leaving him feeling permanently damaged and isolated from others. This belief is reinforced each time a fragment of memory surfaces unexpectedly, reminding him of the horrors he endured and the people he lost. His hopelessness about the future exacerbates his avoidance behaviors. Marco is convinced that discussing what happened or facing certain situations would only intensify these negative feelings and memories. As a result, he has become increasingly withdrawn and reluctant to engage with others, even close friends who do not understand why he has distanced himself. Marco’s daily life revolves around avoiding triggers and trying to cope with the sudden flashes of memory that intrude into his consciousness. These intrusive thoughts and vivid memories make it difficult for him to maintain relationships or focus on work tasks, leading to a cycle where his negative beliefs about himself reinforce his avoidance behaviors and vice versa. The accumulation of these experiences has taken a toll on Marco’s professional life. He has missed several important deadlines at work due to his inability to concentrate during periods when memories intrude, causing stress and potential damage to his career prospects. His social circle has also dwindled as he increasingly isolates himself from friends and colleagues who do not understand the depth of his distress. Despite these challenges, Marco’s hope for a better future remains fragile but present. He is now seeking help because he realizes that his current strategies are not sustainable and that his life feels increasingly constricted by his fears and memories. The most pressing concern for Marco is breaking free from this cycle of avoidance and negative self-appraisals to regain some semblance of normalcy in his daily life and work. Marco’s journey towards healing begins with understanding the profound impact these experiences have had on him, and he hopes that through therapy, he can begin to process his memories without feeling overwhelmed by them. His ultimate goal is to reclaim a sense of identity and hope for the future that has been overshadowed by the traumatic event and its aftermath.
